name: ADR 0001 - Proxmox VE 9 + Talos VM Phase 0
description: Proxmox VE 9 is the host substrate and Talos Linux the Kubernetes node substrate; VLAN 30 is built before Talos so nodes are born on permanent addresses.
content:
# ADR 0001 - Proxmox VE 9 + Talos VM Phase 0

## Status
Accepted

## Context
The earlier redo analysis recommended Talos bare-metal for the old single-node bee-mini framing, and rejected Proxmox because the node was treated as a dedicated, resource-tight Kubernetes appliance. The current rebuild has changed shape: the live target is Proxmox VE 9 on SER8-class hardware, a planned second Proxmox host (pve-evo-x2), VLAN 30 / KubernetesCluster, and Talos VMs instead of a direct bare-metal Talos install. The Proxmox host is already installed and reachable.

## Decision
Use Proxmox VE 9 as the host substrate and Talos Linux as the Kubernetes node substrate for Phase 0. Create VLAN 30 / 192.168.30.0/24 before Talos is built, then run the first Talos control-plane VM on permanent static addressing with the native Talos Kubernetes API VIP. VLAN 30 matches the existing UniFi convention where the VLAN ID maps to the subnet's third octet.

Phase 0 addressing:
- 192.168.30.1  UDM VLAN 30 gateway
- 192.168.30.2  pve-ser8 Proxmox management
- 192.168.30.6  pve-evo-x2 Proxmox management
- 192.168.30.10 Talos native Kubernetes API VIP
- 192.168.30.11 Talos control-plane VM on SER8
- 192.168.30.21 Talos worker VM on EVO-X2
- 192.168.30.200-250 Future ingress / LoadBalancer pool

## Rationale
- Proxmox is already the live host substrate for this rebuild path.
- The live UniFi audit confirms VLAN 30 / 192.168.30.0/24 is free and consistent with the existing LAN/IoT numbering scheme.
- Talos still enforces the no-hand-built-node invariant inside the Kubernetes node boundary.
- Building VLAN 30 first avoids creating Kubernetes on throwaway addresses.
- Talos native VIP avoids adding kube-vip or another load balancer before the cluster exists.
- Reserving service IPs separately from node IPs prevents future ingress and LoadBalancer collisions.

## Consequences
- NORTH_STAR no longer treats Proxmox as rejected for this rebuild.
- Proxmox host setup becomes part of the reproducibility story, not an out-of-band manual sidequest.
- Console/iKVM access is mandatory before management IP or switch-port changes.
- The old bare-metal Talos recommendation is superseded for the current hardware plan but kept as source evidence in docs/history.

name: ADR 0002 - Deploy model: Git-as-plan + Helmfile (CloudNativePG for Postgres)
description: Git is the plan, not a controller - apply is deliberate with Helm/Helmfile and operators own runtime. No GitOps selfHeal. Postgres runs on CloudNativePG (amended by ADR 0010).
content:
# ADR 0002 - Deploy model: Git-as-plan, not GitOps + DB operator

## Status
Accepted (decision #2 amended by ADR 0010 for the Postgres engine).

## Context
The original NORTH_STAR and architecture.md framed the rebuild as a GitOps platform with a controller continuously reconciling and auto-correcting drift (selfHeal). Across the planning conversation that direction changed: a continuous reconciler fights live, stateful, single-operator work and turns every tactical change into a Git ceremony. Patrick has repeatedly and explicitly chosen not GitOps. Separately, the database-operator question was still open.

## Decision
1. Deploy model: Git is the plan, not the enforcer. The repo holds desired state and documentation; we apply it deliberately with Helm/Helmfile, and operators own runtime behavior (failover, scaling, scheduling). We do not run a GitOps controller (Argo CD selfHeal) that continuously reconciles. Drift is made visible (diff, k8sgpt, the agent surface) and corrected on purpose. The anti-drift intent is preserved through visibility + deliberate apply + reproducible-from-git, not through auto-reconciliation.
2. Database operator: Postgres runs on CloudNativePG (amended by ADR 0010 - a bridge for PG19, since KubeBlocks tops out at PG18). KubeBlocks remains the strategic multi-engine operator and runs FalkorDB (graph) plus future engines. One operator family per engine class; fewer moving parts than running every chart separately.

## Rationale
- Not-GitOps removes the reconciler-vs-live-ops conflict and the per-change Git ceremony, while keeping the parts that mattered (declarative, reproducible-from-git, decisions recorded, no silent drift).
- CloudNativePG models many logical databases in one cluster cleanly and is the only operator that runs PG19 today; KubeBlocks stays strategic for FalkorDB and the single-multi-engine-operator endgame.

## Consequences
- NORTH_STAR 'What this is', goal #2, and 'The test' drop selfHeal / continuous reconciliation in favor of Git-as-plan + deliberate apply.
- Argo CD is not the operations brain. If ever reintroduced, it is demoted to baseline-only (no selfHeal).
- In-cluster image build tooling is decided separately in ADR 0005 (Shipwright + BuildKit; Kaniko and hand-rolled build Jobs rejected).
- ADR 0017 amends the no-hand-apply rule to permit agent-driven mutation through a scoped Kubernetes MCP server.

name: ADR 0006 - Declarative substrate + platform delivery (one Helmfile, maintained charts)
description: Stop hand-rolling the bootstrap: OpenTofu provisions VMs, talhelper versions Talos config, one Helmfile applies the platform from pinned maintained Helm charts. State changes only through git then apply.
content:
# ADR 0006 - Declarative Substrate and Platform Delivery

## Status
Accepted (item 3 + 3a amended - Helm-chart presumption + manifest exception clause).

## Context
Phase 0 (ADR 0001) was brought up by hand: qm commands created VM 110, talosctl gen config produced and patched controlplane.yaml, the node was bootstrapped, and Cilium was installed imperatively at a terminal. The resulting node config is declarative, but the process that built it exists only as prose plus an agent's command history. 'Rebuild the cluster from git' (NORTH_STAR goal 3) is therefore not yet true. This is precisely the hand-rolling the NORTH_STAR non-negotiable ('install and configure, never hand-roll') forbids, occurring at the substrate layer, and it had already begun creeping up into the platform (Cilium was hand-installed, not declared).

## Decision
1. VM provisioning is OpenTofu + bpg/proxmox. Every VM (Talos nodes, the HAOS VM) is declared in git and created/changed with tofu apply. No hand qm.
2. Talos config is talhelper + SOPS. A single talconfig.yaml in git plus a SOPS-encrypted talsecret.sops.yaml; talhelper genconfig produces the machine configs on demand. Node configuration is under version control with secrets encrypted in git.
3. Platform delivery is one Helmfile, applied through git. platform/helmfile.yaml declares every platform layer (Cilium, cert-manager, ESO+Doppler, Longhorn, CloudNativePG, KubeBlocks, ingress, cloudflared, Shipwright+Tekton) with pinned versions and values. The default install path for any new platform component is its upstream maintained Helm chart, with overrides as a values file under platform/values/. The only way a Helm-managed platform component is installed or updated is helmfile apply.
3a. Exception for components without a maintained Helm chart. When, after a documented search, no maintained and versioned Helm chart exists, the component may be applied as a pinned manifest under its domain directory, recorded by an ADR amendment to this rule with a top-of-file EXCEPTION header. Recorded exception: Garage (ADR 0012) - in-cluster S3, no maintained versioned chart exists.
4. The rule: state changes only through git then apply (tofu apply / talhelper / helmfile apply). No hand qm, kubectl apply, helm install, or live edits. Drift is made visible deliberately (helmfile diff, k8sgpt) and reconciled on purpose.
5. Retrofit, do not rebuild. The live Phase 0 node stays; it is captured into OpenTofu + talhelper + the Helmfile so the next plan/diff is a no-op against it, then proven with a rebuild-from-git test.

## Rationale
- These are the homelab-standard, maintained packages for declarative Talos-on-Proxmox (bpg/proxmox is current for PVE 9.x; talhelper is the accepted way to version Talos config with SOPS; Cilium-on-Talos via cni: none is documented by Sidero). Adopting them is 'install, don't hand-roll' applied to the substrate itself.
- It turns the weak prose runbook into code, which is the difference between 'we wrote about how we did it' and 'we can re-do it with a command.'
- It stops the hand-rolling at the node layer before it metastasizes into the platform layer, which is how the previous cluster decayed.

## Consequences
- controlplane.yaml / worker.yaml become generated output (gitignored), not hand-authored sources of truth; the source of truth is talconfig.yaml + the SOPS secret.
- Repo grows three top-level dirs: tofu/, talos/, platform/.
- Cilium (hand-installed at 1.16.0) is re-managed via the Helmfile; the version pin bumps to current stable there.
- Components without a maintained Helm chart (Garage, ADR 0012) are applied as pinned manifests with an ADR exception and an Install path entry in the capability-registry; the Helmfile carries a pointer to each manifest exception.
- A SOPS age key and a Doppler ClusterSecretStore become bootstrap prerequisites (documented, not in git).

name: ADR 0011 - App deployment standard (apps as manifests, copy _template)
description: Apps from many repos share one repeatable deployment contract: app repos own code + Dockerfile + a Shipwright Build; runtime manifests live centrally under apps/<app>/, copied from apps/_template/.
content:
# ADR 0011 - App Deployment Standard

## Status
Accepted

## Context
Apps from multiple repos (MooseGoose, TechDeals, a robot-factory, others) need a single, repeatable way to deploy onto the cluster and connect to the shared databases, so each app is not a snowflake (the false-green failure mode in the previous cluster history). The platform exists (Gateway, cert-manager, cloudflared, ESO/Doppler, Shipwright, the CNPG/KubeBlocks databases), but the deployment contract an incoming repo follows was undocumented.

## Decision
1. App repos own code + Dockerfile + a Shipwright Build. Runtime manifests live centrally in this repo under apps/<app>/ (one source of truth for cluster desired state; git then apply, ADR 0002/0006).
2. Three workload shapes: web/API (Deployment + Service + HTTPRoute), worker (Deployment), and scheduled batch (CronJob/Job). The copy-paste template is apps/_template/.
3. Reachability via the shared Cilium Gateway (ADR 0007); public hostnames egress through cloudflared; TLS via cert-manager.
4. Config/secrets via ESO from Doppler; images by digest from Shipwright (ADR 0005).
5. Databases are shared clusters (pg18/pg19/falkordb); apps connect per docs/connection-registry.md (the cluster -rw service + a per-app role + a Doppler key). No per-app database server.
6. The authoritative guide is docs/deploying-apps.md; the database contract is docs/connection-registry.md.

## Rationale
- Centralizing runtime manifests in one repo gives a single source of cluster state for a solo operator, which beats each repo owning its own deploy/ and self-applying (more drift, more moving parts).
- A copy-paste template plus a documented contract means an incoming app agent reads the docs and produces a conforming apps/<app>/ bundle without re-deriving the platform integration each time.
- Shared database clusters with per-app roles match the 'adding a database is trivial' NORTH_STAR goal: a new logical DB is a few-line CNPG Database entry, never a new server.

## Consequences
- Implementation folders hold manifests only; all prose/standards live in docs/. apps/_template/ is the bundle; per-folder READMEs are removed.
- An incoming app agent reads docs/deploying-apps.md + docs/connection-registry.md and produces a conforming apps/<app>/ bundle; AGENTS.md routes it there.
- The alternative (each repo owns its own deploy/ and self-applies) is rejected for a solo operator: more drift, more moving parts, no single source of cluster state.
